The challenge involves creating a web-based tool, open to the public, that allows anyone to observe these changes in the sky in a visual and intuitive way.
Why is it important?
It is important because it allows for the observation of changes in real time and generates over a billion observations; it can also be used for planetary defense.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? 

SPHEREx Atlas functions as a virtual observatory within a web browser; users can simply open a webpage-without needing to install any software-to see how the infrared sky changes between the passes of NASA’s SPHEREx mission.

What benefits does it have?

The benefits include zero development costs; it is open-source, replicable, and scalable, and it can benefit the educational sector as well as technical sustainability.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The project’s anticipated impact includes enabling the analysis of data-which would be impossible to process manually-concerning invisible moving objects, addressing a gap in educational access, and providing users with the opportunity to discover new things in outer space.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The programming languages ​​and technologies used to develop the project are HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, and the Canvas API.

How is your project creative?

A project that gives the user the opportunity to explore the outdoors on their own is creative.

What factors did your team consider?

The factors my team took into account include alignment with the official NASA challenge, use of NASA’s open data, accessibility and usability, modular architecture and technical design, transparency and documentation, economic viability and scalability, and educational and social impact.
